BASHFORTH2016.title: A Middle Pennsylvanian macrofloral assemblage from wetland deposits in Indiana
BASHFORTH2016.note: Primary taxonomic study, pp606-608 Fig10 specimens USNM594376-594379: six to nine whorled leaves, cuneate toothed and divided forms; hooked leaves known from other cuneifolium material, absent in these particular fossils. Consult-only copyright, no copied pixels/meshes/textures in model.
BASHFORTH2016.pixels: Fig10 actual rendered page607 inspected; cuneate and divided foliage distinguished from unrelated ferns on same plate.

BSPG2015.title: Stammscheibe eines Baumfarns
BSPG2015.note: Primary museum specimen SNSB-BSPG2002XV255 Psaronius simplex crosssection plus cited Taylor2009 whole-plant reconstruction Fig1. Adventitious root mantle thickens at base; crown shown with compound arching fronds. Whole model stays genus-level, not a species-level association claim. Consult-only copyright, no copied imagery in model.
BSPG2015.pixels: Museum crosssection and reconstruction both personally viewed. Thin core with root-mantle support and upright tree-fern habit.

STOCKEY2006.title: Relationships among fossil and living Dipteridaceae: anatomically preserved Hausmannia from the Lower Cretaceous of Vancouver Island
STOCKEY2006.note: Primary author-uploaded full paper accessed through ResearchGate. Hausmannia morinii S59519A/S59518B Fig1a/b half-lamina with paired rounded teeth and reticulate veins; Fig1c/d shows bifurcating major veins. Reconstruction is isolated preserved fan sector, no complete parent. Copyright2006 University of Chicago; consult-only, no redistribution of source pictures or incorporation.
STOCKEY2006.pixels: Actual full-paper page653 Fig1 viewed, including asymmetrical continuous fan sector, paired rounded teeth and net veins; earlier downloaded ResearchGate fig1 was paperFig2 anatomy and is retained with this correction.

BODNAR2018.title: Middle Triassic dipterid ferns from west-central Argentina and their relationship to palaeoclimatic changes
BODNAR2018.note: Primary reexamination of Dictyophyllum castellanosii BAPb6227 part/BAPb6228 counterpart, p401 Fig3. Two rachial arms, each4-5 linear-lanceolate pinnae, short basal web, lobate-serrate margins, reticulate veins. Choose these named specimens, not unnamed genus montage. Source pixels remain consult-only, no incorporation.
BODNAR2018.pixels: Actual p401 figure3 part and counterpart personally inspected. Open pinna gaps and basal fan divergence directly visible.
